title: Broker hardening: concurrent termination idempotence, detached-grandchild kill proof, acceptance
description:
SPIDR child 3d of 4, split from task-af3d7bc8af2146cf92d98557ed0e90c0 by architect-5aba94da. Human confirmed the 4-way split in the REPL. Carries parent DoD items 5 and 6. This is the LAST child, so it owns the whole-parent hardening gate: full regression across the broker package, the integration coverage below, and the final adversarial pass.

DEPENDS ON task-05bf0e0fe7e84afb8584588ecf96db14 (3a), task-14ab762db8494959b93b070b9d3b3730 (3b) and task-55e2c4c836894a788b7a30960e4fdb1f (3c). Do not start until all three are DONE, and RE-MEASURE their landed symbols before planning -- every prior task in this chain found a stale claim in its own description.

Objective: prove the containment guarantee actually holds when things go wrong at the same time, and that a killed broker still cannot strand a process tree.

Deliverable, inside packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/:
- tests/idempotence.rs (NEW): foreground integration tests asserting CANCEL, fd0 EOF and an instructed timeout arriving CONCURRENTLY still terminate and reap exactly once. 3c proves each path individually; this proves they cannot double-fire when they race. Drive them genuinely concurrently rather than sequentially -- a test that serialises them proves nothing this task exists for.
- tests/real_broker.rs (NEW): the acceptance sweep, including the kill proof below.

THE KILL PROOF IS THE POINT OF THIS TASK. Launch a provider that itself spawns a DELIBERATELY DETACHED grandchild, then forcibly terminate the broker. Closing the last Job handle must kill BOTH the parent and the detached grandchild. Prove death by PID PLUS CREATION TIME for each -- a bare PID is reused by Windows and a PID-only check can report a stranger's process as "dead". Ordinary controlled paths must additionally record ActiveProcesses==0.

Also prove that NO provider output can be parsed as broker control: feed the provider bytes that are byte-identical to a well-formed control frame on fd4/fd5 and assert they never reach the control path and never influence a status frame. This is the confused-deputy case the fd separation exists to prevent, and it is the one most likely to be quietly untested.

CONSUMER EDGE, required by the epic's pure-package rail clause 1(a): record task-4d1f8ba54cb6476c930c46b413f882aa ("Windows Job Object provider process boundary") as the Node consumer that will compose this broker. As measured 2026-08-10, NO Node-side consumer exists yet -- grep across packages/ for the broker name or a six-entry stdio array returns nothing. Do NOT build one here; naming it satisfies the rail.

NOT IN SCOPE: building the Node consumer, JavaScript object/path/environment/output-bound validation, Claude discovery/grants, daemon/store orchestration, receipts, public @moe/runner exports.

Verification: cargo test --locked --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-broker && cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-broker
definitionOfDone: Foreground integration tests drive CANCEL, fd0 EOF and an instructed timeout CONCURRENTLY -- genuinely racing, not serialised -- and assert termination and reaping happen exactly once, by a call-count table. A test that merely runs the three paths one after another does not satisfy this item; 3c already covers the sequential case.

A provider that spawns a DELIBERATELY DETACHED grandchild is launched, then the broker is forcibly terminated. Both the parent AND the detached grandchild are proved dead by PID PLUS CREATION TIME for each -- never by PID alone, since Windows reuses PIDs and a PID-only check can report an unrelated live process as the dead one.

Ordinary controlled completion and cancel paths record Job ActiveProcesses==0 before returning, distinguishing them from the forcible-kill path where last-handle close is the mechanism. Both are asserted; neither is inferred from the other.

Provider bytes that are BYTE-IDENTICAL to a well-formed control frame are written to fd4/fd5 and proved never to reach the control path and never to influence any fd1 status frame. The assertion is on the control path's recorded input, not merely on the absence of a crash or an unexpected status.

The full broker suite passes as a regression -- every test from 3a, 3b and 3c still green and unweakened, verified by mutating one production surface per sibling and confirming the corresponding suite goes red. The locked broker test and release-build commands both exit 0 on this supported Windows host.

The broker consumes moe-windows-job-core without duplicating its Win32 authority, verified by grep for CreateJobObject, AssignProcessToJobObject, CreateProcessW, ResumeThread, TerminateProcess and WaitForSingleObject call sites in broker sources; and task-4d1f8ba54cb6476c930c46b413f882aa is recorded as the Node consumer per the pure-package rail.

Every Rust production source is <=250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` with counts recorded; no executable, Cargo target output, transcript, generated smoke evidence, or probe artifact is committed, and any process or temp path a test creates is cleaned up on every exit path including panic.
taskRails: Prove process death by PID PLUS CREATION TIME, never by PID alone. Windows reuses PIDs, so a PID-only check can report an unrelated live process as the dead one -- that is a false green, not a shortcut.
Concurrency must be genuine. Serialising CANCEL, EOF and timeout defeats the entire purpose of this task; drive them so they actually race.

Closing the last Job handle is crash safety, not success evidence. Controlled paths must query ActiveProcesses==0; only the forcible-kill path may rely on last-handle close, and the two must be asserted separately.
Provider bytes on fd3/fd4/fd5 are never mixed with or parsed as control. The confused-deputy case must be tested with bytes that are byte-identical to a valid control frame.
Import moe-windows-job-core; restate no Job or process syscall in the broker.

Tests must actually run on this win32 host -- no #[ignore], no cfg gate, no stub. Clean up every spawned process and temp path on every exit path including panic; never commit target output, binaries, transcripts or smoke evidence.
As the final child, this task owns full broker-package regression and the whole-parent adversarial pass, not just its own slice.
